name: Learn basic contact juggling
blurb: The ball never leaves your body — it rolls, glides and floats. The foundation moves are the palm isolation and the butterfly, and both look supernatural long before you are actually good.
gear: A 75–100 mm acrylic or stage ball
A soft surface to drop onto
steps: Learn the palm balance: hold the ball still on your flat palm and move your whole body around it.
Learn the isolation: rotate your hand around the ball so the ball appears to hang motionless in space. Practise against a fixed background reference.
Learn the butterfly: roll the ball from your palm over the back of your hand and catch it back in the palm, in one continuous motion.
Practise both hands and both directions from the start.
Learn the head roll or arm roll as a transition between hands.
Link isolation, butterfly and a roll into a slow 20-second sequence.
tips: Contact juggling is slow. Any speed you add is hiding a mistake.
Acrylic balls focus sunlight and can start fires and burn hands. Never leave one in the sun.
proof: You hold a convincing isolation for ten seconds while your hand visibly rotates around the ball.
